headline: Trump Says Revised GDP Numbers ‘Fake,’ Calls for Investigation
author: Josh Wingrove

paragraphs.text: Thu, November 26, 2026 at 10:03 AM EST 2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- President Donald Trump accused his own administration of a "purposeful" move to under-report US economic growth, seizing on a routine data revision to underpin an allegation of election interference with no evidence.

In a social media post on Thursday, Trump pointed to GDP figures that showed the economy grew 4.3% annualized in the third quarter — revised from the 3.4% estimate in a previous release — saying it's a "major difference."
"It was just revealed that the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE," he said without offering proof.

"I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation. This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error," the president added in the post, which was sent from his West Palm Beach golf course on the morning of the US Thanksgiving holiday.
Trump has long stoked fringe or conspiratorial explanations for election defeats, though has previously chalked up this month's midterm rout to the fact he was not personally on the ballot.
The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes GDP figures in stages, and the headline number often moves as the agency factors in additional data.
Trump has complained about unflattering economic numbers in the past. Last year, he fired the head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics after a report showed weak job growth.
